newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the tenth consecutive session on Tuesday but analysts said the dominant buying after price fixing signalled the market would rise on Wednesday after having fallen 14.6 percent since October 9.
"After such a fall the market had to react," said Aleksander Jawien of Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.

Analysts said the two-week fall represented profit-taking after the market had risen about 100 percent this year, but said that selling accelerated after parliament's lower house passed a bill last week cutting taxes for low earners, seen as possibly increasing the budget deficit and thereby inflation.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.1 percent to 12,873.3 points and turnover inched up two percent to 96.7 million zlotys ($34.4 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 57 to 14 with nine stocks flat.
Analysts said it was not clear how the market would react after Wednesday's prospective rebound, though Andrzejewski saw strong support between 12,300 and 12,600 points.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of falls by brewer Zywiec and construction firm Elektrobudowa by or near 10 percent.

They said construction firm Espebepe, which fell 9.1 percent and did not trade after price-fixing due to excess supply, was still suffering from last week's news it could go bankrupt if creditors did not agree on a debt write-off deal.
Continuous trade turnover rose to 2.7 million zlotys ($1 million) from Monday's 1.1 million ($0.4 million) with biggest mover food trader and producer Animex up 5.8 percent.

NFI units fell 5.4 percent in the regular bourse session in a 24-million-zloty turnover ($8.5 million) but rose 1.8 percent in 19.4-million-zloty ($6.9 milliion) continuous trade, and analysts said stronger post-price-fixing buying could signal a rebound.
